narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 39% probability that you would become a bad credit risk. In lending terms, that is the estimated chance of repayment difficulty, and it was above the risk level the lender was willing to accept. The most influential factor was your savings information: with no known savings, this factor nevertheless leaned in your favor rather than pushing toward bad risk. The second most influential was your checking-account status; having no checking account also counted toward lower risk. The third and strongest factor pushing the other way was the amount requested: about 7,980 DM, far above the roughly 3,020 DM average among approved applicants. That large request, together with your 36-month term versus about 19 months typically approved, your installment rate near 4% versus about 3%, and less than one year of employment, raised the overall risk estimate enough to deny the loan. To improve a future application, reduce the amount requested and consider a shorter term, build a documented savings and checking relationship with the bank, and provide evidence of steadier employment or income. You may also review your credit history for errors before reapplying.
